Exit reasons

Exit-logic variant sweep (SOXX)

In-sample sensitivity on SOXX — five exit configurations swept against the original spec. Demonstrates that the 2× ATR stop was the binding constraint.

Entry-delay sweep (SOXX)

Entering k trading days after the signal fires, instead of next-bar open. Tests the "signal fires after short-term overbought, entry is too early" hypothesis.

Trend-filter sweep (SOXX)

Take signals only when SOXX is above its 200-day MA at the signal date. Applied independently to two exit configs.

Split-half OOS (SOXX, train / test 2022-09-08)

Within-SOXX out-of-sample test: pick the variant by train-half Sharpe, report test-half stats.

Tuning verdict

Loading…

Best per-ETF configuration — across every variant tested

For each ETF, the strongest config from the base×thrust grid (items 1+4), continuous signal (item 2), 50/100 + master-regime overlay (item 3), and the prior Test 1/2/3 batch. Sharpe is the selection criterion; buy-and-hold row shown for reference.

Base × thrust Sharpe grid (per ETF)

Annualised Sharpe across base allocation (rows: % always in the ETF) × thrust allocation (columns: % held when the breadth signal is active). Greener = higher Sharpe. The signal works when greener cells sit OFF the bottom row (signal alone) and OFF the diagonal (no leverage).

—

Continuous signal (smooth allocation in [base, 1])

Replaces the binary in-trade/out-of-trade state with a continuous score: allocation = 0.5 + 0.5 × clip((composite_z − p10) / (p90 − p10), 0, 1). Smoother turnover, no on/off flips.

Master regime filter (CSP1 breadth overlay on 50/100)

When SPY breadth is unhealthy (composite_z < expanding p10 OR ma_breadth < 0.40), force allocation to zero across every sector. Shows whether a market-wide veto reduces sector drawdowns enough to justify the cost.

OOS validation of the 50/150 SOXX winner

Split the SOXX signal-eligible window at 2022-09-08. Sweep the full base × thrust grid on the TRAIN half only; pick the winner by train-half Sharpe; apply that same config without re-tuning to the TEST half. If the train-half winner holds up OOS, the parameter selection is robust across regimes (the train half includes COVID + the 2022 inflation shock; the test half includes the AI rally + Apr-2026 sell-off).
